title: Intel is handing its Atom chip tech to a startup run by the CEO’s longtime partner
excerpt: Intel is quietly handing one of its crown jewels to a tiny, stealthy startup. And that startup is run by a longtime business partner of Intel’s own chief executive. The chipmaker is giving RosaicLabs access to its Atom processor technolog
content_html:
Intel is quietly handing one of its crown jewels to a tiny, stealthy startup. And that startup is run by a longtime business partner of Intel’s own chief executive.

The chipmaker is giving RosaicLabs access to its Atom processor technology, according to a source and documents reviewed by Reuters. Atom is the building block of its central processors. It is a rare move for Intel, which almost never licenses pieces of its x86 architecture.

Rosaic is led by Amarjit Gill, a veteran chip executive and venture investor. He and Intel boss Lip-Bu Tan are longtime co-investors. The pair helped build the founding team at Rivos, a chip startup that Meta bought last year, outbidding Intel, while Tan was its chairman. Both also backed Nuvia, later sold to Qualcomm.

What Intel is actually handing over

The transfer is not trivial. Intel aims to ship Rosaic the register-transfer level (RTL) code for Atom. That is the low-level blueprint describing how the chip works.

It gives a customer deep exposure to Intel’s intellectual property, one veteran chip executive said, enough to build their own custom designs. Atom itself is built for low power and low heat, which suits mobile and edge devices.

Rosaic is barely public. It filed its first Delaware incorporation papers in May and has no website or LinkedIn page, as is common for chip startups working in secrecy. Its founding team includes veterans of Rivos, and an amended July filing shows it can raise a $10m seed round.

Why it looks awkward

The optics are the story. Intel is deep in a hard turnaround under Tan, who has pushed aggressive cost-cutting and tried to open up its foundry to outside customers. Licensing its IP is part of that plan.

But handing rare access to a company run by the chief executive’s former investment partner, staffed by alumni of the startup that once outbid Intel, invites obvious questions. Reuters has previously reported on deals that boosted Tan’s personal fortune. Intel declined to comment, and Gill did not respond.

There is a strategic logic, too. Intel rarely shares its x86, and opening Atom to a nimble startup could seed markets it cannot chase alone. Rivals are already racing to build custom silicon for the AI era. Whether that outweighs the governance questions is what Intel’s board, and its investors, will have to weigh.

content_html_zh:
英特尔正在悄然将其皇冠上的一颗明珠交给一家小型、隐秘的初创公司。 这家初创公司是由英特尔首席执行官的一位长期业务合作伙伴经营的。

据路透社查阅的消息人士和文件称，这家芯片制造商正在向 RosaicLabs 提供其 Atom 处理器技术的使用权。 Atom 是其中央处理器的构建模块。 对于英特尔来说，这是一个罕见的举动，因为英特尔几乎从未授权其 x86 架构的各个部分。

Rosaic 由资深芯片高管和风险投资者 Amarjit Gill 领导。 他和英特尔老板 Lip-Bu Tan 是长期共同投资者。 两人帮助组建了 Rivos 的创始团队，Rivos 是一家芯片初创公司，Meta 去年以高于英特尔的价格收购了该公司，而 Tan 担任该公司董事长。 两家公司都支持 Nuvia，后来被卖给了高通。

英特尔实际上正在移交什么

这次转移并非小事。 英特尔的目标是为 Rosaic 提供 Atom 的寄存器传输级 (RTL) 代码。 这是描述芯片工作原理的低级蓝图。

一位资深芯片高管表示，它让客户深入了解英特尔的知识产权，足以构建自己的定制设计。 Atom 本身专为低功耗和低热量而设计，适合移动和边缘设备。

罗萨克几乎不公开。 该公司于 5 月份提交了第一份特拉华州公司注册文件，没有网站或 LinkedIn 页面，这对于秘密工作的芯片初创公司来说很常见。 其创始团队包括 Rivos 的资深人士，7 月份修改后的文件显示，它可以筹集 1000 万美元的种子轮资金。

为什么看起来很尴尬

光学就是故事。 在谭先生的领导下，英特尔正陷入艰难的转型，他推动了积极的成本削减，并试图向外部客户开放其代工厂。 授权其知识产权是该计划的一部分。

但向首席执行官的前投资合伙人经营的公司提供罕见的访问权，其员工都是这家曾经出价高于英特尔的初创公司的校友，这会引发明显的问题。 路透社此前曾报道过增加谭个人财富的交易。 英特尔拒绝置评，吉尔也没有回应。

这也是有战略逻辑的。 英特尔很少分享其 x86，向灵活的初创公司开放 Atom 可能会为其无法单独追逐的市场带来种子。 竞争对手已经开始竞相为人工智能时代打造定制芯片。 这是否比治理问题更重要，是英特尔董事会及其投资者必须权衡的问题。
